items.title: Body-Size Indexation of Left Atrial Volume in Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction: Retrospective Reclassification and E/e' Concordance.
items.abstract: To determine whether associations between body mass index (BMI) and left atrial (LA) size differ when LA volume is expressed as absolute volume, indexed to body surface area (BSA), or indexed to height squared, and whether discordant classification is associated with E/e' in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF). This retrospective observational study linked MIMIC-IV and MIMIC-IV-ECHO. The complete-indexation cohort comprised 1663 adults with a documented heart failure diagnosis, left ventricular ejection fraction ≥50%, and required body-size and LA measurements. Multivariable models evaluated BMI associations with absolute LA volume, LAV/BSA, and LAV/height 2 . Discordance was defined as BSA-normal but height 2 -enlarged; adjusted E/e' was compared with the group normal by both methods. BMI was positively associated with absolute LA volume (β = 0.345; 95% CI, 0.124-0.567), inversely associated with LAV/BSA (β = -0.329; 95% CI, -0.456 to -0.203), and positively associated with LAV/height 2 (β = 0.156; 95% CI, 0.077-0.236). Discordant classification occurred in 389 of 1663 participants (23.4%). Adjusted E/e' was 1.630 higher (95% CI, 0.738-2.522) than in participants normal by both methods. The absolute reclassification proportion decreased to 9.6% with an alternative published height 2 threshold. Body-size normalization materially changed apparent LA enlargement in this selected HFpEF population. BSA-normal/height 2 -enlarged classification was associated with higher E/e', a noninvasive filling-related marker, but was threshold-dependent. These findings do not establish diagnostic superiority or prognostic benefit.

items.title: Dapagliflozin vs. Acetazolamide in Patients With Acute Heart Failure: A Randomized Controlled Trial (CHOICE-AHF).
items.abstract: Early adjunctive therapies may improve decongestion and symptoms in acute heart failure. This trial compared dapagliflozin with acetazolamide when initiated early, focusing on dyspnea relief as the primary outcome and decongestive, diuretic, natriuretic, and safety outcomes. In this randomized, active-controlled trial, 108 adults hospitalized with acute heart failure, dyspnea, and objective evidence of congestion requiring intravenous loop diuretics were randomized to receive dapagliflozin 10 mg (N = 55) or acetazolamide 500 mg (N = 53) once daily for 3 days alongside standard care. The primary endpoint was the between-group difference in 72-hour dyspnea visual analog scale area under the curve. Secondary endpoints included successful decongestion within 3 days, diuretic and natriuretic responses, the relative change in N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide levels from baseline to day 3, and safety. Acetazolamide produced a significantly lower 72-hour dyspnea area under the curve than dapagliflozin (2647.9 ± 1213.8 vs. 2988.7 ± 1196.7 mm × hour; P = 0.048). It increased cumulative urine output over 72 hours (12,200 vs. 10,000 mL; P = 0.019) and total natriuresis over 48 hours (824.7 vs. 547.9 mmol; P = 0.001). Dapagliflozin achieved a larger reduction in N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide at 72 hours (-34.2% vs. -25.0%; P = 0.003). Safety events were infrequent and similar. In conclusion, acetazolamide provided greater dyspnea relief, diuresis, and natriuresis, whereas dapagliflozin produced a larger short-term reduction in N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide. Further studies are needed to validate these findings. Trial registration: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06783166.

items.title: Left Atrial Strain and Left Atrio-Ventricular Coupling in Heart Failure Patients with Left Ventricular Hypertrophy and Wild-Type Transthyretin Cardiac Amyloidosis.
items.abstract: Wild-type transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis (ATTRwt-CA) is a cardiomyopathy characterized by myocardial and atrial stiffening. We aimed to assess left atrial (LA) function and left atrio-ventricular coupling index (LACI) in heart failure (HF) patients with left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH) and evaluate their ability to discriminate ATTRwt-CA from non-amyloid LVH. We conducted a case-control study including 50 patients with ATTRwt-CA and 50 HF patients with hypertensive heart disease. LA reservoir strain (LARS), LA contraction strain (PACS), LA stiffness index (LASI), LA reservoir work (LAWr) and LACI have been measured. Propensity score matching (PSM) was performed for interventricular septal thickness (IVS), relative wall thickness (RWT), age, sex, coronary heart disease (CAD) to mitigate confounding. Before matching,  significant differences in IVS, RWT, age, sex, and CAD rates were observed between cases and controls. After PSM, LA functional indices remained significantly impaired in CA patients compared to controls. In the multivariate analysis, only LARS and LASI were independently associated with ATTRwt-CA. A LASI > 1.57 (AUC 0.87) and a PACS  ≤  6.0% (AUC 0.79) demonstrated the highest diagnostic accuracy for identifying ATTRwt-CA, with reduced LARS ( ≤  14.0%) also providing significant discrimination. Incorporating LASI  into the AMYLI (AUC 0.91) and IWT scores (AUC 0.89)  significantly enhances overall diagnostic accuracy for ATTRwt-CA detection. LA function and the atrio-ventricular coupling are more impaired in ATTRwt-CA patients compared to patients with HF alone; especially LARS and LASI are independent predictor for ATTRwt-CA and should be assessed in HF patients with LVH to detect CA.

items.title: Bicuspid Aortic Valve With Preserved Ejection Fraction: One-Year Changes in Ventricular and Atrial Mechanics.
items.abstract: Left ventricular (LV) dysfunction in bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) disease may precede ejection fraction (EF) decline. We assessed 1-year changes in LV global longitudinal strain (GLS), left atrial (LA) strain and myocardial work in BAV with preserved EF. This retrospective cohort included 82 adults with BAV and sinus rhythm who had preserved LVEF (≥50%) at two echocardiograms 363 ± 15 days apart without interim surgery; 40 age- and sex-matched controls with tricuspid aortic valves were imaged once. Primary outcomes were changes in absolute GLS and LA reservoir strain (LASr); myocardial work, corrected for the transaortic gradient in aortic stenosis, was exploratory. Reader reproducibility was tested on stored images. At baseline, patients had lower absolute GLS (17.8 ± 2.8% vs. 21.8 ± 1.0%) and LASr (38.5 ± 5.2% vs. 40.8 ± 3.4%) than controls (p < 0.001 and p = 0.004). At 1 year, mean LVEF and LV volumes did not change significantly, whereas absolute GLS decreased by 0.8% points (95% CI 0.5-1.1) and LASr by 2.4 points (1.7-3.0; both Holm-adjusted p < 0.001). Gradient-corrected global work index decreased by 47 mmHg% (27-68). The GLS decrease exceeded the intra-observer minimal detectable change in 22 patients (27%), versus an increase in 4 (5%). The GLS change was not significantly associated with valve lesion type or severity. In selected patients with BAV who maintained preserved LVEF without valve or aortic surgery, LV GLS and LA reservoir strain decreased slightly over 1 year. Their clinical significance requires validation with longitudinal controls and test-retest data.

items.title: Acral melanoma: a unique subtype requiring unique solutions.
items.abstract: Acral melanoma (AM) is a 'rare-by-rare' melanoma subtype arising on the volar skin of the palms, soles, or nail apparatus. Unlike sun-exposed cutaneous melanoma (CM), AM has a low mutational burden but extensive structural genomic alterations, including clustered copy number events ('hailstorms'/tyfonas) that contain amplification of oncogenes such as CCND1 and TERT. Mechanical stress and distinct clonal evolution, with late, often subclonal, MAPK mutations, may mediate AM development and progression. Nevertheless, AM management is largely extrapolated from CM. Benefits of immunotherapy and targeted therapies remain unclear due to limited trial enrollment and under-representation of diverse patient populations. In this review, we integrate current knowledge with critical challenges in AM research and outline priorities to accelerate AM-specific discoveries and treatments, close critical knowledge gaps, and improve patient outcomes through global collaboration.

items.title: DV-Based Kidney-Sparing Therapy for High-Risk Upper Tract Urothelial Carcinoma: An Exploratory Single-Center Real-World Study.
items.abstract: To evaluate the feasibility, safety, and renal functional outcomes of a disitamab vedotin-based kidney-sparing therapy (DV-based KST) combining ureteroscopic holmium laser ablation with disitamab vedotin (DV, HER2-targeted antibody-drug conjugate) and immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) in high-risk upper tract urothelial carcinoma (UTUC). This retrospective, single-center exploratory study included 11 patients with HER2-expressing high-risk UTUC treated with DV-based KST. A source cohort of 101 patients with high-risk UTUC who underwent RNU was identified, from which 44 patients were selected by 1:4 balance-constrained optimal matching as an exploratory reference cohort. The primary outcome was kidney preservation, defined as avoidance of salvage RNU. Secondary outcomes included composite clinical response, local recurrence patterns, exploratory OS, renal function changes, and safety. Median follow-up was 21.0 and 36.0 months in the DV-based KST and RNU groups, respectively. Composite clinical response rates were 100%, 90.9%, and 81.8% at 3, 6, and 12 months, respectively. Kidney preservation rates were 90.9% at 6 months and 72.7% at both 12 and 18 months. Most recurrences were low-grade Ta-stage lesions and were managed endoscopically. Exploratory OS analysis did not detect a statistically significant difference between the matched cohorts (log-rank P = .40). Mean eGFR change was + 0.9% in the DV-based KST cohort versus - 10.9% in the matched RNU cohort (P < .001). No grade 4 or treatment-related fatal adverse events occurred. DV-based KST appeared feasible in highly selected patients with HER2-expressing high-risk UTUC who were unsuitable for or unwilling to undergo RNU. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require prospective multicenter validation.

items.title: Early discontinuation of immune checkpoint inhibitors after objective response in real-world melanoma: Clinical and economic impact.
items.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have transformed outcomes in advanced melanoma, but optimal treatment duration remains unclear. Most patients are treated until two years, treatment limiting toxicity (TLT), or progression. This study evaluates real-world outcomes after elective discontinuation of ICIs following treatment response based on national recommendations. Data from the Danish Metastatic Melanoma Database (DAMMED) were retrieved on all patients who initiated first-line ICI therapy (anti-PD1 +/- anti-CTLA4) between January 2019 and July 2023. All patients who discontinued treatment after a maximum of 18-months due to complete response (CR) or partial response (PR) were included while patients stopping due to progression, TLT or other causes were excluded. In total, 163 patients were included (63% male, median age 71 [33-91]). Most had cutaneous melanoma (85%), M1c disease (42%), and received anti-PD1 (80%). Overall, 82 and 81 patients discontinued following CR and PR, respectively. Median and minimum treatment duration was 8.1/7.1 months (CR), and 11.1/8.9 months (PR). The median follow-up was 48 months [IQR: 34.6-60.1]. At 12- and 36-months, PFS was 100%/87% (CR), and 96%/81% (PR). At 12- and 36- months, OS was 99%/98% (CR) and 100%/87% (PR). Melanoma-specific survival (MSS) at 12- and 36 months was 100%/99% (CR) and 100%/93% (PR). Early discontinuation following an objective response is associated with an excellent 3-year MSS and a potential significant reduction in treatment expenses. These findings suggest that, in selected responding patients, treatment discontinuation before the 2-year landmark may be feasible without compromising outcomes, supporting response-guided discontinuation strategies.

items.title: Retraction notice to "A novel machine learning model for efficacy prediction of immunotherapy-chemotherapy in NSCLC based on CT radiomics" [Computers in Biology and Medicine 178 (2024) 108638].
Severe pembrolizumab-induced lichenoid mucositis with durable complete response in recurrent head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.
items.abstract: Severe oral mucosal immune-related adverse events are uncommon complications of immune checkpoint inhibitors and may compromise treatment continuation in patients with head and neck cancer. A 77-year-old man with recurrent/metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma and a PD-L1 combined positive score of 95 developed grade 3 oral mucositis after six months of pembrolizumab. Histopathological findings were compatible with immune-mediated lichenoid mucositis associated with anti-PD-1 therapy. Systemic corticosteroids achieved complete clinical resolution. However, mucositis recurred after pembrolizumab rechallenge, leading to permanent treatment discontinuation. Complete radiological response was subsequently documented and persisted for more than one year after treatment cessation. This case highlights the importance of early recognition and multidisciplinary management of severe oral immune-related toxicity. Rechallenge may result in recurrent severe mucositis, while durable oncological remission may persist after immunotherapy discontinuation.

Transplantation of Hepatitis B Surface Antigen Positive or Viremic Kidneys: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
items.abstract: This systematic review and meta-analysis examines the evidence related to the use of HBV positive kidneys into non-viremic kidney transplant recipients (KTRs). We searched PubMed and Embase through November 2025 and identified studies of recipients of hepatitis B surface antigen positive (HBsAg+) or viremic kidneys. Studies with a comparison group of KTRs of HBV negative kidneys that reported on patient and allograft survivals were included in the meta-analysis. The risk ratios (RR) for patient and allograft survivals were pooled to obtain the estimate and 95% confidence interval, at 1-, 3-, and 5-years post-transplant. Viral transmission including HBsAg development, HBV viremia, or hepatitis was also reviewed. Eleven studies were included in the systematic review and 6 in the meta-analysis. They included 638 KTRs of HBV positive kidneys and 2800 recipients of HBsAg negative non viremic kidneys. At 1, 3, and 5 years, the RR of allograft survival was not statistically different between the 2 groups and was 1 [0.98-1.01], 1.01 [0.98-1.04], and 1.00 [0.91-1.09] respectively. Similarly, the RR of patient survival was comparable between the 2 groups. The rate of HBV transmission was low (4.94%), especially when prophylaxis was used and when recipients were immune pre transplant. Kidneys from HBV infected donors confer similar patient and allograft survival than those from HBV negative donors. They may be used to expand the donor pool, in immune KTRs and with appropriate prophylaxis, in light of this emerging evidence of safety with very low reported rates of transmission.

items.title: SUMOylated DDX3 Promotes HBV Replication and Tumor Growth of Hepatocellular Carcinoma via TRIM28-DDX3-KLF4α Signaling Axis.
items.abstract: DDX3 has dual biological functions of regulating cell proliferation and antiviral effects. Herein, we focus on SUMOylation-mediated DDX3 in the interplay from hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection to HBV-associated hepatocellular carcinoma (HBV-HCC) progression. We identified dynamic regulation of SUMOylation and DeSUMOylation of DDX3 at four key lysine (K) residues (K81/K208/K215/K564) in response to HBV infection. During the early stage of HBV acute infection, SENP1 interacts with DDX3 to keep DDX3 deSUMOylation for inhibiting HBV replication. During persistent HBV replication, as SENP1 downregulation and HBV polymerase accumulation, DDX3 disassociates with SENP1 to bind with TRIM28, which induces DDX3 SUMOylation. Meanwhile, SUMOylated DDX3 enhances alternative splicing of KLF4 mRNAs to generate KLF4α isoform that involves in Cyclin D1-mediated cell cycle progression, weakens tumor suppressor function of DDX3 and promotes HBV-HCC. Moreover, DDX3 expression is positively correlated with KLF4 mRNA, and high DDX3 level with low TRIM28 expression indicates a better overall survival for HBV-HCC patients. Our findings reveal the dynamic regulation between SUMOylation and deSUMOylation of DDX3, including mediating HBV gene transcription, virus antigen secretion, and cell proliferation. Furthermore, the TRIM28-DDX3-KLF4 axis as a novel therapeutic target for HBV-HCC, exhibiting the dual ability to inhibit tumor progression and disrupt the HBV-host interaction.

items.title: Risk factors for thiopurine-related toxicity in Latin American inflammatory bowel disease patients.
items.abstract: Thiopurines continue to play a role in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) treatment, particularly in resource-limited countries. However, there are scarce data from Latin America regarding thiopurines-associated AE. We aim to describe the thiopurine-associated AE and determine risk factors for its occurrence. Clinical data from IBD patients treated with thiopurines in a Chilean tertiary centre were retrospectively collected including AE that required thiopurine withdrawal and weight-based thiopurine dose. A multivariable model was fitted to determine independent risk factors of thiopurine-related AE. Odds ratios (OR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) were calculated. A total 163 out of 587 (27.7%) patients discontinued thiopurine treatment due to AE including myelosuppression, hepatitis, pancreatitis, and gastrointestinal intolerance. Multivariate analysis showed that older age (OR: 1.02; 95% CI: 1.01-1.04; p=0.01) and lower body weight (OR: 0.97; 95% CI: 0.95-0.99; p=0.01) were independent risk factors for thiopurine-associated AE. Discontinuation of thiopurines due to AE is frequent in Latin IBD patients. Particular caution should be exerted in older and low-weight IBD patients starting thiopurine treatment.
items.journal: Revista de gastroenterologia del Peru : organo oficial de la Sociedad de Gastroenterologia del Peru

items.title: Beyond HIV prevention: Reframing PrEP clinics as hubs for viral hepatitis prevention and elimination.
items.abstract: The expansion of HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) has created a growing network of prevention services that regularly engage people who may also be exposed or susceptible to viral hepatitis. PrEP care is inherently longitudinal, involving repeated clinical assessment, laboratory testing, counselling and vaccination review. These features make PrEP clinics uniquely positioned to contribute to viral hepatitis prevention and elimination. In this narrative review, we synthesize evidence on the integration of viral hepatitis prevention, screening, diagnosis and care within PrEP services, and propose a practical framework, the PrEP-viral hepatitis elimination cascade, for translating the principle of integrated HIV, viral hepatitis and sexually transmitted infection services into routine clinical practice. A focused literature search was conducted between 1 May and 8 August 2026 across PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus and the WHO Global Index Medicus, using documented search strings supplemented by hand-searching of reference lists. We prioritized studies conducted among PrEP users or within PrEP programmes, together with relevant international guidelines and policy documents. Records were screened in two stages against predefined eligibility criteria, and the findings were mapped to the steps of the cascade. Evidence was sought on HAV and HBV vaccination coverage, HBV seroprevalence and susceptibility, the relationship between tenofovir-based PrEP and HBV prevention, HCV epidemiology among PrEP users, simplified diagnostic strategies and integrated service delivery models. Given the heterogeneity of study designs and outcomes, the literature was synthesized narratively rather than through formal meta-analysis. Interventions and indicators for each cascade step were then summarized in an evidence-linked implementation and monitoring table. The evidence consistently demonstrates that vaccination gaps for HAV and HBV persist among PrEP users, with suboptimal initiation and completion rates across settings; that HBV susceptibility remains common among individuals entering PrEP care; and that tenofovir-based PrEP, while offering incidental HBV protection, should not substitute for vaccination. HCV epidemiology among PrEP users is heterogeneous, supporting risk-adapted testing strategies, while simplified diagnostic pathways and self-testing approaches have shown promise for HCV. The PrEP-viral hepatitis elimination cascade proposed here offers a structured, implementable framework connecting vaccination, case finding, linkage to care and longitudinal reassessment within the existing PrEP pathway. The cascade is presented as a detailed figure and as an implementation and monitoring table linking each step to supporting evidence, candidate interventions and measurable indicators, without assigning responsibilities to specific providers. Implementation challenges include variability in PrEP delivery models, the need for equity-oriented approaches and the implications of long-acting and tenofovir-sparing PrEP regimens for HBV prevention. PrEP programmes have created a longitudinal prevention infrastructure that extends beyond HIV prevention. HAV vaccination, HBV screening and vaccination, identification of chronic HBV infection, HCV testing, simplified diagnostics, treatment linkage and surveillance for reinfection can all be incorporated at different points of the PrEP pathway. The next step is to move from opportunistic to intentional integration. PrEP clinics should be reframed as integrated viral hepatitis prevention and elimination hubs, translating global strategies into routine care and contributing to viral hepatitis elimination goals. The question is no longer whether PrEP clinics can contribute to viral hepatitis elimination, but whether the global health community will deliberately invest in making this integration a reality.

items.title: 18 F-FGln PET/CT Imaging of Glutamine Uptake Has Potential for Predicting Immunotherapy Response in Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
items.abstract: We investigated whether glutamine (Gln) uptake, imaged by 18 F-(2S,4R)-4-fluoroglutamine ( 18 F-FGln) PET/CT, could predict and modulate immunotherapy response in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Analysis of the Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA)-Liver Hepatocellular Carcinoma (LIHC) dataset revealed that SLC1A5 expression-which encodes a primary Gln uptake channel in HCC cells-was significantly associated with poor prognosis, higher tumor grade, and an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. In murine HCC models, tumors with high 18 F-FGln uptake exhibited elevated Slc1a5 expression and poor response to anti-PD-1 therapy, whereas low-uptake tumors were more sensitive to immunotherapy. Genetic knockdown of Slc1a5 reduced 18 F-FGln uptake, enhanced anti-PD-1 efficacy, increased cytotoxic T lymphocyte infiltration, and decreased regulatory T cell abundance. Transcriptomic and single-cell analyses revealed activation of antitumor immune pathways and reprogramming toward an immune-inflamed phenotype after Slc1a5 suppression. V-9302 decreased tumor Gln uptake, as measured by 18 F-FGln PET/CT, and sensitized HCC to PD-1 blockade. In patient-derived organoid-T cell co-culture systems, low-SLC1A5 organoids were susceptible to PD-1 blockade, whereas high-SLC1A5 organoids were resistant, consistent with 18 F-FGln PET/CT findings. These results identify Gln uptake as a checkpoint of immune evasion in HCC and support that 18 F-FGln PET/CT has the potential to predict and monitor immunotherapy response.

items.title: Diagnostic Performance of Magnetic Resonance Elastography Versus Vibration-Controlled Transient Elastography for Liver Fibrosis Staging in Steatotic Liver Disease.
items.abstract: Gravitational magnetic resonance elastography (GT-MRE) enables comprehensive biomechanical liver characterization and may overcome limitations of conventional elastography techniques. This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of two- and three-dimensional (2D and 3D) GT-MRE compared with 2D acoustic MRE (AC-MRE) and vibration-controlled transient elastography (VCTE) for liver fibrosis staging. In this prospective study, patients with suspected or known steatotic liver disease underwent GT-MRE (2D and 3D, gradient-echo sequences) and AC-MRE (2D, spin-echo echo-planar imaging) at 1.5 T, plus VCTE with a median interval to MRE of 37 days (IQR, 20-124 days; range, 0-372 days). Statistical analyses included generalized additive models, ordinal logistic regression, and decision tree-based classification. Diagnostic performance was assessed using cumulative receiver operating characteristic analysis and corresponding areas under the curve (AUCs). Ninety-one participants (median age, 55 years [IQR, 45-64]; 41 women) were included, of whom 35 (38%) had histopathological correlation. In the biopsy-confirmed subgroup, 3D GT-MRE-derived viscoelastic parameters showed promising exploratory performance for early fibrosis classification. Wave attenuation achieved AUCs of 0.91 for F0 versus ≥ F1 and 0.99 for ≤ F1 versus ≥ F2, while phase angle yielded an AUC of 0.88 for F0 versus ≥ F1, with numerically higher AUCs than conventional stiffness-based metrics. For advanced fibrosis thresholds, all modalities performed well (AUC ≥ 0.84). Obuchowski measures for 3D-derived parameters were 0.95-0.96. Internally cross-validated multiparametric modeling achieved an accuracy of up to 92%. VCTE measurements plateaued beyond F3, whereas AC- and GT-MRE metrics continued to increase with fibrosis severity. 3D GT-MRE-derived viscoelastic parameters showed promising performance for liver fibrosis classification and provided biomechanical information complementary to conventional stiffness measurements. Given the limited biopsy-confirmed sample and marked class imbalance at F0, these findings require validation in larger independent cohorts before clinical implementation.

items.title: A novel preclinical platform to study FGFR2 fusion-driven cholangiocarcinoma ☆ .
items.abstract: FGFR2 fusions represent the most frequent genetic alteration in intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (iCCA). However, clinical responses to FGFR inhibitors are suboptimal. A major limitation is that preclinical models do not mimic the immunobiology of human FGFR2-driven iCCA. We developed an autochthonous and immunocompetent FGFR2 fusion-driven mouse model. Using the hydrodynamic tail-vein injection method, we generated a mouse model harboring the FGFR2-PPHLN1 fusion (with or without the V565F resistance mutation) in combination with activated YAP1, and established 2D lines and 3D organoids. We characterized tumors using bulk and single cell RNA-sequencing (n=3), spectral cytometry (n=3-7/group), and performed cross-species analysis using 411 human samples. Tumor-associated neutrophils (TAN) were depleted in vivo using an anti-murine Ly6G antibody. In vitro and in vivo drug treatment with FGFR inhibitors and anti-PD-L1 was performed. FGFR2-driven murine tumors were molecularly and immunologically similar to human iCCA, with selective accumulation of TAN and impaired T cell infiltration. scRNA-seq identified pro-tumorigenic and immunomodulatory TAN subsets while In vivo TAN depletion significantly prolonged survival (log-rank p=0.009) and led to increased CD8 + T cells infiltration (p=0.007). 3D organoids reproduced clinical responses to irreversible FGFR inhibitors, while showing a sustained response to the reversible inhibitor derazantinib in presence of the V565F mutation (IC50=5.190uM). In vivo derazantinib reduced tumor number (unadj. p=0.03) and marginally prolonged survival (unadj. p=0.052) whereas no statistically significant benefit of anti-PD-L1 was detected, either alone or in combination. Our mouse model faithfully recapitulates the immunobiology and therapeutic sensitivities of the human disease. Inter-species and cross-species analyses suggest a critical role of FGFR2 fusions in shaping a cold tumor microenvironment with selective accumulation of TAN in both humans and mice. This study develops a clinically-relevant mouse model of FGFR2-driven iCCA for future translational studies. Accumulation of pro-tumorigenic and immunomodulatory TAN along with poor sensitivity to immune checkpoint inhibitors suggests the need of designing alternative strategies harnessing the unique immunosuppressive nature of these tumors.

items.title: Beyond bacteria: A fungal metabolite drives liver cancer from within.
items.abstract: Gut bacteria are established drivers of steatotic liver disease and liver cancer-gut fungi, much less so. Zhou et al. show that Rhizopus arrhizus promotes MASLD-associated liver cancer through kynurenic acid, a metabolite that bypasses its own surface receptors to engage the cytoplasmic scaffold IQGAP1.

items.title: Longitudinal Pancreatic Imaging Findings in BRCA1 , BRCA2 , ATM, and PALB2 Heterozygotes Undergoing Pancreatic Cancer Surveillance: A Prospective PRECEDE Consortium Study.
items.abstract: Imaging surveillance for pancreatic cancer (PC) is recommended for select high-risk individuals (HRIs) with a goal of downstaging PC diagnosis and improving long-term survival. A common subgroup of HRIs undergoing PC surveillance imaging includes those with a heterozygous pathogenic germline variant (PGV) in breast cancer susceptibility genes BRCA1 , BRCA2 , ATM , or PALB2. Despite expanding recommendations for PC surveillance imaging in these individuals, limited evidence exists to guide counseling regarding the frequency and longitudinal outcomes of imaging findings. The Pancreatic Cancer Early Detection (PRECEDE) Consortium is a prospective multicenter cohort study of HRIs undergoing PC surveillance imaging. In this study, we report imaging outcomes across the first 5 years of enrollment (April 2020-April 2025) for PRECEDE participants with a heterozygous PGV in BRCA1 , BRCA2 , ATM , or PALB2 . Among 2,085 eligible participants, PGVs in BRCA2 (51%) were most common, followed by BRCA1 (21%), ATM (19%), and PALB2 (9%). Baseline pancreatic imaging occurred primarily with endoscopic ultrasound (EUS; 55%) or magnetic resonance imaging (43%). More than half (54%) of the participants had at least 1 pancreatic imaging finding during the study, while concerning findings including worrisome cysts, main pancreatic duct dilation ≥5 mm, and solid masses were detected in 9.1% of the cohort. Among HRIs without a pancreatic cyst or solid mass at baseline imaging, 71% remained without findings after at least two follow-ups. Additionally, 87% of HRIs with pancreatic cysts and follow-up imaging using the same modality did not have worrisome cyst growth. In this largest reported cohort of BRCA1 , BRCA2 , ATM , and PALB2 heterozygotes undergoing PC surveillance imaging, benign/low-risk pancreatic imaging findings were common and stable on short-term follow-up, providing important data for counseling these HRIs.
